newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian government wins confidence vote.
newsitem.headline: Italian government wins confidence vote.

text.p: Italy's centre-left government won a vote of confidence in parliament on Wednesday which it had called to ram through a decree covering a rescue plan for the ailing southern bank, Banco di Napoli.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi called the vote in the lower house of parliament to sweep aside 1,001 amendments to the decree proposed by the separatist Northern League party which had been blocking its passage into law.

The vote in the Chamber of Deputies, where Prodi depends on the hard left Communist Refoundation party for support, was 316 to 286, officials said. A second vote will now take place on Thursday to pass the decree itself into law.
The Treasury wants to inject two trillion lire ($1.3 billion) of state funds into Banco di Napoli and privatise the heavily indebted bank before the end of the year.
The decree had been set to expire on November 24. It cannot be resurrected after that as a result of a recent Constitutional Court ruling which prevents decrees from being resubmitted.

The confidence vote was the second the government has faced since taking office in May. Prodi called, and won, a confidence vote in August to ram a mini-budget into law, with the legislation again being threatened by League obstructionism.
